business.business_description: Shreeji Auto Components Limited manufactures precision-machined engine and transmission components for two-wheeler and passenger-vehicle original equipment manufacturers. The Company operates two manufacturing facilities at Rajkot, Gujarat, with an aggregate installed capacity of 6.2 million components per annum.
business.products_services: Machined camshafts, rocker arms, transmission shafts, hubs and forged sub-assemblies supplied to OEM and tier-1 customers, together with a replacement-market range distributed through regional dealers.
business.revenue_model: Revenue is earned under annual rate contracts and long-term supply agreements with original equipment manufacturers and their tier-1 suppliers, billed on despatch, supplemented by a smaller aftermarket and replacement-parts channel sold through distributors.
business.industry_overview: The Indian auto-component industry supplies both domestic vehicle assembly and the export replacement market. Demand for precision machined components is linked to two-wheeler and passenger-vehicle production volumes, to the pace of engine and transmission localisation by original equipment manufacturers, and to steel input prices. Industry participants in the precision machining segment typically compete on quality system certification, delivery reliability and the ability to co-develop components with the customer's engineering team.
business.top_customers: 1) Hero-tier supplier ABC Limited — 28% of revenue; 2) Rico-tier supplier DEF Limited — 22%; 3) GHI Forgings Limited — 14%; 4) JKL Motors Limited — 9%; 5) MNO Auto Private Limited — 6%.
business.suppliers: Forged blanks are sourced principally from Shreeji Forgings LLP, an entity owned by the promoters, and from two third-party forging houses in Rajkot. Alloy steel is procured from secondary steel distributors on spot terms.
business.plants_capacity: Rajkot Plant I (Plot 42, GIDC Industrial Estate) — installed capacity 3.8 million components per annum, utilisation 81% in FY26. Rajkot Plant II (Plot 117, Metoda GIDC) — installed capacity 2.4 million components per annum, utilisation 68% in FY26.
business.employees: 312 permanent employees as at 31 March 2026, comprising 41 in engineering and quality, 236 in production and 35 in administration and support, together with contract labour engaged on a shift basis.
business.competitive_strengths: IATF 16949 certified quality systems across both plants; an established supply relationship of over eight years with its two largest customers; in-house tool room reducing changeover time; proximity to the Rajkot forging cluster.
business.business_strategies: Commission a third machining line at Rajkot Plant II to serve committed volumes; broaden the customer base to reduce concentration on the two largest accounts; increase the share of higher-margin transmission components; pursue approval as a direct-tier supplier to a passenger-vehicle original equipment manufacturer.
business.mda_drivers: Revenue grew over the three-year period principally on higher despatch volumes to the two largest customers and the commissioning of additional machining capacity at Plant II. Margins were affected by alloy steel price movements, which are only partially passed through under annual rate contracts, and by a higher share of contract labour. Working capital remained elevated because OEM customers settle on 60 to 90 day terms while forging suppliers are paid within 45 days.
business.internal_notes_for_checker: Customer concentration is high — the top two customers together account for 50% of revenue. A GST input-credit demand of INR 1.15 crore relating to FY 2023-24 is currently under appeal before the Appellate Authority. Forged blanks are purchased from Shreeji Forgings LLP, a promoter-owned entity.
business.intellectual_property: The Company holds a registered trademark for its word mark in class 12 (registration granted 2019). It holds no patents. Tooling designs used on the machining lines are maintained as confidential know-how and are not separately registered.
business.immovable_properties: Rajkot Plant I at Plot 42, GIDC Industrial Estate is held on a 99-year lease from the Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation, with 87 years remaining. Rajkot Plant II at Plot 117, Metoda GIDC is held on a 99-year lease with 91 years remaining. The registered office is situated within Plant I. The Company owns no freehold immovable property.

financials.peer_comparison: The Company's board considers that no directly comparable listed peer of similar scale operates in the precision machined two-wheeler component segment on the SME platform. For reference, listed auto-component companies of substantially larger scale traded at a price-to-earnings multiple in the range of 18 to 26 times trailing earnings as at the date of this draft. Investors are cautioned that these companies differ materially in scale, product mix and customer profile.
